questiontext.text:
{@E[1]@}

Type \(\le\) as <= and \(\ge\) as >=, for example 4x+9y<=72. Use the letters x and y as defined in the question.

(a) Write the inequality for {@rw1@}.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Write the inequality for {@rw2@}.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) Find the whole-number plan that gives the greatest profit. \(x =\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] \(y =\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]

[[feedback:prt3]]

(d) The greatest profit is Ksh [[input:ans5]] [[validation:ans5]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) \({@ta1@}\) (b) \({@ta2@}\), with \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\) and whole numbers.

(c) The boundary lines meet at the vertex \({@vd@}\), the best corner of R for \(P = {@pp@}x + {@pq@}y\). [[if test='isint']]It is a whole-number point, so it is the answer.[[else]]It is not a whole-number point, so test the whole-number points of R around it and check every constraint.[[/if]] The best plan is \(x = {@bst[1]@}\), \(y = {@bst[2]@}\).

(d) \(P = {@pp@} \times {@bst[1]@} + {@pq@} \times {@bst[2]@} = {@t@}\), so the greatest profit is Ksh \({@thou(t)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: maximum profit from a situation

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (d) / Essential 1.4 (d): Write two resource constraints from a situation, then find the whole-number plan with the greatest profit and that profit.

Core and Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 8, Exercise B, question 5 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: two inequalities from a situation and the most profitable whole-number plan, with Kenyan contexts and new numbers.
